To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electron-probe system is a complex object that is difficult to automate.

1) the electron-probe system is a unique tool for scanning large areas (up to 1 cm2) at high resolutions (3–20 nm); 2) the parameters of the electron-probes system can be selected to optimize the information obtained; 3) it is possible to automate the selection of parameters and the real-time mode of control during scanning.
the electron-probe parameters of the template for imprint lithography can be controlled in the real time by using a special program.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the automation of the mode of the template control of imprint lithography.

the development of an algorithm for the real-time control and adjustment of the parameters of the electron-prope systems of a scanning electron microscope during the acquisition of images with the required resolution.
a new approach to solving the problems of automating the electron-probe systems for imprint lithography.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electron-probe system is a very complex system that can be controlled only in real time.

the electron probe system is an important and necessary component of the imprint lithography template fabrication process, which must be considered in the design and implementation of the template fabrication process.
the electron beam is a versatile tool for the fabrication and characterization of nanostructures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results presented in this paper are of great practical importance and will be used in the development and implementation of the next generation of electron-probe instruments.

we were able to develop the necessary theoretical foundations for the automation of the electron-prope system control, and we were able to demonstrate the practical application of these foundations in the development of an electron-probe system for scanning large areas with high resolution.
the electron-probe systems can be used as a universal tool for scanning areas on the scale of 1–2 cm2 with a spatial resolution of 10 nm and a time resolution of 1–10 μs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the optimum mode for the scanning of a template can be found in the course of the experiment, which is the most important feature for the development of fully automated systems for imprint lithography.
the electron-probe parameters can be controlled in real time by using the dependence of the electron-probing current on the scanning speed.
the parameters of the scanning system can be controlled in the process of data acquisition.
